latest_rss.title: Why does 'eat well' mean so much in China?
latest_rss.summary: How do you get to know China from abroad? For many, it begins somewhere unglamorous: a Chinese restaurant on a street corner. There's an old joke that wherever people go, a Chinese restaurant follows. It's an exaggeration, of course, but quite a telling one, as it speaks to a culture that has spent centuries perfecting the art of the meal, and to something quieter still: the way a modest table, set anywhere in the world, can carry the full weight of someone's hope for a decent life.The film Once Upon a Time in the Middle East opens on exactly this kind of table. latest_rss.title: Beijing Signals Tiered Governance of Open-Weight Models
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Beijing is converging on a “tiered governance” approach to open weight models, under which basic capabilities would be released freely, frontier capabilities would face security review, and the most sensitive models would be confined to only domestic use.



Support for open weights is a deliberate response to constraints. It offsets a compute deficit that leaves the People’s Republic of China (PRC) roughly two years behind the United States according to leading Chinese AI founders, gives domestic chipmakers a model to optimize against, and exploits the absence of any U.S. legal tools for regulating published weights.



Open weights serve Beijing’s security priorities, which treat sovereignty and development as core components of its expansive view of national security. Possession of the weights is what allows government, financial, and military users to run models offline on classified data, free from a foreign provider that could cut off access at any time.
